name: Health Information Technician, Coder and Medical Office Administrator
description: ⚠⚠⚠ Three different routes wear this name in Florida, they are taught at roughly the same number of institutions, and only ONE of them leads to the field's professional credential. Health information management — 31 institutions, and the associate degree is what makes you RHIT-eligible. Billing and coding — 37 institutions and the largest output, all clock-hour certificates, none of which does. Medical office administration — 36 institutions into an occupation of 850,000 people with no credential ladder at all. ⚠⚠ Choosing wrongly does not waste a term; it forecloses the credential.
credentialNote: ⚠⚠⚠ RHIT ELIGIBILITY REQUIRES AN ASSOCIATE DEGREE, AND NO CERTIFICATE SUBSTITUTES. AHIMA's rule: you must have completed the academic requirements, at associate degree level, of a Health Information Management programme accredited by CAHIIM. ⚠⚠ AHIMA also states that HEALTH INFORMATICS degrees are NOT currently accepted for RHIT — so the newer, more technical-sounding degree is the wrong one, and that is a real and expensive mistake. Verify CAHIIM accreditation with CAHIIM, not with the school. ⚠⚠⚠ AND ON THE CODING SIDE, WHAT YOU EARN IS AN APPRENTICE CREDENTIAL. Pass AAPC's CPC examination without qualifying experience and you hold CPC-A: the A is for apprentice, and removing it takes TWO YEARS of verified on-the-job coding experience, or ONE year plus AAPC's Practicode or its 80-hour course. ⚠ Employers advertising for a CPC usually mean one without the A — so the credential you need a job to earn is the credential the job asks for. ⚠⚠ Ask any coding programme how its graduates break that circle: a real externship, an employer relationship, or Practicode in the price. A programme with no answer is selling you an examination. ⚠ Nothing on any of these three routes is licensed by Florida. The credential is the whole gate, which is why which one you can reach matters so much.
bodyHtml:
⚠⚠⚠ Three routes, one name, and only one ladder

RouteFL institutionsFL credentials (2023)What you getCredential it reaches
Health information management31296 — 109 associate degreescollege CREDIT (HIM1xxx/HIM2xxx)✅ RHIT, then RHIA
Billing and coding⚠ 37⚠ 416 — all certificatesCLOCK HOURS (HIM0xxx)⚠ CPC — but see CPC-A
Medical office administration36242 — all certificatesclock hours⚠⚠ none

⚠⚠⚠ The route with the WIDEST footprint and the MOST graduates is the one that cannot produce an RHIT. A coding certificate is a real qualification for a real job — but no quantity of it becomes a degree, and the degree is what the profession's credential is built on.

⚠⚠ Florida writes the answer into the course numbers

Number rangeWhat it isExample
HIM0xxx⚠ CLOCK HOURS — the certificate routesHIM0091 Medical Coder/Biller 1, 350 hours
HIM1xxx / HIM2xxx✅ COLLEGE CREDIT — the CAHIIM associate degreeHIM2253 CPT Coding, 9 institutions
HIM3xxx / HIM4xxxthe bachelor's, at FAMU, UCF, USF, UWF, FGCU, Santa Fe, St Petersburg and Florida PolyHIM4218 Electronic Health Records and Health Data

⚠ The level digit is the map. If a programme you are offered is numbered HIM0, it is clock hours, and clock hours do not become a degree by themselves. Ask in writing what will articulate before you enrol, not after.

The occupations

RoleSOC2025 medianEmployedOpenings/yrGrowth 2024–34
Medical records specialist29-2072$51,140194,80014,200✅ much faster than average (7%+)
Medical secretary / admin assistant43-6013$45,930⚠⚠ 850,000⚠⚠ 85,900average (3–4%)

⚠⚠ The front-office occupation is more than four times the size of the records one and has six times the annual openings. It is much easier to get into and it pays about $5,200 less, and — the part that matters over a career — it has nowhere to go.

⚠⚠ The automation question, answered with the actual number

Everyone considering coding asks whether artificial intelligence will end it. The federal projection does not support that: BLS projects medical records specialists to grow 8 percent from 2025 to 2035, much faster than the average for all occupations, and O*NET agrees at 7% or higher.

⚠ What is changing is the shape of the work, not its quantity. Computer-assisted coding proposes codes and a human validates, corrects and defends them — which moves value toward auditing, denials and clinical documentation improvement, where the question is whether the chart supports the code. Florida already numbers that specialism: HIM3240 CDI Principles and Practice and HIM3243 Coding and Reimbursement for CDI Professionals, both upper division at Santa Fe and St Petersburg.

⚠⚠ So the defensive move is not to avoid coding — it is to aim past pure production coding at audit and CDI, which needs the degree.

⚠ Two coder/biller programmes, 110 hours apart

Florida runs the coder/biller certificate as a three-course clock-hour block, and there are two active statewide families:

FamilyHoursFL institutions
HIM0091–0093 Medical Coder/Biller 1–3350 + 350 + 320 = 1,02015
HIM0071–0073 (marked OCP B)300 + 300 + 310 = 9107

⚠ Five institutions carry both. Add HIM0009 Introduction to Health Information Technology (90 hours, 18 institutions) and the programme runs roughly 1,000 to 1,100 clock hours either way. Ask which family your programme uses and what the total is; the difference is about three weeks.

⚠ A state title still naming a code set retired in 2015

The statewide title on HIM2222 is Basic ICD-9-CM Coding. The United States retired ICD-9-CM for diagnosis and procedure coding on 1 October 2015.

✅ The carriers are current and the state record is not — Miami Dade, St Petersburg and State College of Florida title it ICD Coding Systems, and Palm Beach State, Tallahassee and Valencia title HIM2222C Applied Inpatient Coding. Florida also numbers ICD-10 work separately at HIM2722, HIM2723 and HIM2724.

⚠⚠ The practical instruction: judge a coding course by the code set on its syllabus, never by the number or the state's title. Ask which code sets and which year's guidelines — ICD-10-CM, ICD-10-PCS, CPT and HCPCS Level II — because coding guidelines change annually and a course running on old ones is worth much less than one that is not.

Necessary skills

  • Reading a clinical record for what it actually documents, not what you assume happened. This is the whole job, and it is harder than it sounds.
  • Precision with classification systems — ICD-10-CM, ICD-10-PCS, CPT, HCPCS — and the discipline to look it up rather than recall it.
  • Anatomy, physiology and pathophysiology at a level that lets you tell whether a code fits a diagnosis.
  • HIPAA and the law of the record. The medical record is a legal document and you are its custodian.
  • Willingness to query a physician when documentation does not support a code — the core of clinical documentation improvement, and the skill that separates a coder from an auditor.
  • Comfort with software that is often bad, because the electronic health record is where you will live.

Advice

⚠⚠⚠ Decide which of the three routes you are on before you pay anyone. They are taught at the same colleges, with similar names, at similar prices, and they end in different places. If there is any chance you will want the RHIT, start on the associate degree.

⚠⚠ Verify CAHIIM accreditation with CAHIIM. And do not accept a health informatics degree as a substitute — AHIMA says plainly that it is not one.

⚠⚠ On the coding route, ask about the CPC-A before anything else. Externship, employer relationship or Practicode — one of those three, or you will finish the programme holding an apprentice credential with no way to remove it.

⚠ Look for a credentialing examination review course in the plan — HIM2960, carried by five institutions. A programme that builds toward the examination is aimed at the credential; one that does not is aimed at the certificate.

And if you are already working the front office, you are better placed than you think. You know how a practice runs, which is the part programmes cannot teach — adding the associate degree is a shorter distance for you than for anyone starting fresh.

programs.note: ⚠⚠⚠ The only one of the three that reaches the profession's credential. 31 Florida public institutions, 296 credentials, 109 of them associate degrees — and the associate degree from a CAHIIM-accredited programme is what RHIT eligibility requires. ⚠ Read its degrees note on why a health informatics degree will not do instead.

⚠⚠ The widest footprint — 37 Florida institutions, 416 credentials — and every one a clock-hour certificate, so none of it makes anybody RHIT-eligible. ⚠ A real qualification for a real job; just not a rung on the ladder. Read its note on the CPC-A apprentice trap before enrolling.

⚠ The largest job market of the three (850,000 medical secretaries and administrative assistants nationally, 85,900 openings a year) and the only one with no credential ladder at all. ⚠⚠ Easy to enter — 48% of entrants have a high school diploma — and hard to leave, which is why the page recommends treating it as a starting point rather than a purchase.

⚠ Named because it competes for the same students at the same technical colleges and covers the same administrative work (MEA0501 Medical Office Procedures, MEA0334C Medical Coding and Insurance Billing) PLUS a clinical half. ⚠⚠ It also has four labelled exit points where these routes have none, so it keeps more doors open if you are undecided.

⚠ Not a route into these jobs — but the reverse move is real and underadvertised. Health information departments hire experienced clinicians into clinical documentation improvement and coding audit, where understanding what a chart MEANS outranks coding speed. ⚠⚠ One of the few desk-based second careers a nurse can reach without starting over.

courses.reason: Introduction to Health Information Technology — 90 clock hours, 18 institutions. The shared entry block of Florida's clock-hour health-information certificates: the record, its law, its privacy and its vocabulary.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Clock hours, not credit. If a degree may follow, ask what will articulate before you start.

courses.reason: Medical Coder/Biller 1 — 350 clock hours, 15 institutions. The first third of the larger of Florida's two coder/biller families.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠ TWO active statewide families: HIM0091–0093 at 350+350+320 = 1,020 hours (15 institutions) and HIM0071–0073, marked OCP B, at 300+300+310 = 910 hours (7). Five institutions carry both. Ask which yours runs.

courses.reason: Medical Coder/Biller 2 — 350 clock hours, 15 institutions. Diagnosis and procedure coding in practice.
Medical Coder/Biller 3 — 320 clock hours, 15 institutions. Reimbursement, claims and the denial cycle, which is where coding actually meets money.
Introduction to Health Information Management — 15 institutions, and the first course of the CREDIT route. ⚠ If your catalogue offers you this rather than HIM0009, you are on the degree track.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Four institutions carry the integrated HIM1000C instead.

courses.reason: Legal Aspects of Health Information Management — 14 institutions, the second most widely carried credit course in the prefix. HIPAA, release of information, retention, subpoenas, and the record as a legal document.
CPT Coding — 9 institutions. Procedural coding, and the code set outpatient and physician billing runs on.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Five institutions carry the integrated HIM2253C instead.

courses.reason: ICD-10-PCS Coding — 7 institutions. Inpatient procedure coding, the hardest of the code sets and the one hospital reimbursement turns on.

⚠⚠ ICD Coding Systems — 3 institutions, with 3 more carrying HIM2222C as Applied Inpatient Coding. Named here for a warning: the STATEWIDE title on this number still reads Basic ICD-9-CM Coding, a code set the United States retired on 1 October 2015.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠⚠ The carriers are current and the state record is not. Judge a coding course by the code set on its syllabus and the guideline year — never by the number or the statewide title.

courses.reason: Health Statistics — 8 institutions. Case-mix index, length of stay, mortality and morbidity rates: the reporting a health information department produces and the reason the job is analytic rather than clerical.
Supervision and Organization — 10 institutions. The supervisory content that distinguishes the degree from the certificate, and the reason the degree leads somewhere.

Directed Practice II — 8 institutions, and where several run it as revenue-cycle work. ⚠ The professional practice experience is also the thing most likely to solve the CPC-A experience problem, so ask what it involves.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Placement means Florida Level 2 background screening and HIPAA training — start them in week one of the term before.

courses.reason: ⚠ Credentialing Exam Review — 5 institutions. A programme that carries this is aiming its students at the RHIT examination rather than at a certificate, which is exactly the signal to look for.

⚠⚠ CDI Principles and Practice — upper division, Santa Fe and St Petersburg. Clinical documentation improvement is where the field is moving as computer-assisted coding takes over production work, and Florida already numbers it.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Upper division, so it needs the associate degree first — another reason the degree route matters.

courses.reason: Electronic Health Records and Health Data — upper division at UCF and UWF. The bachelor's-level treatment, on the route to RHIA.
Medical Terminology — 16 institutions. Unavoidable: you cannot code or abstract a record you cannot read.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Florida numbers this twice: HSC1531 at 16 institutions and HSC2531 at 8.

courses.reason: Business Communications — 10 institutions. The front-office route's most widely carried credit course, and the skill a practice actually hires on.

Anatomy and Physiology I — 20 institutions. ⚠ Coding accuracy rests on anatomy; several HIM programmes substitute their own HIM1453 Medical Records Anatomy and Physiology, which is credit but transfers less widely.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Two equivalent packagings: BSC2085 plus BSC2085L at 20 institutions, combined BSC2085C at 7. Take the general version if a further degree is possible.

sources.label: O*NET — Medical Records Specialists (29-2072.00)
sources.note: 194,800 employed (2024), growth much faster than average (7% or higher), 14,200 annual openings, median $51,140 (2025). Education 52% high school diploma, 22% postsecondary certificate, 13% some college. Tasks include compiling and maintaining records, identifying and coding patient data using standard classification systems, protecting record security, reviewing for regulatory compliance, and assigning diagnosis-related groups.

sources.label: BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook — Medical Records Specialists
sources.note: ⚠ Quoted on the page because it answers the automation question with a number: employment is projected to grow 8 percent from 2025 to 2035, much faster than the average for all occupations, about 14,000 openings a year, median $51,140 (May 2025). ✅ BLS and O*NET AGREE here, which is not always the case. Typical entry-level education: postsecondary nondegree award.

sources.label: O*NET — Medical Secretaries and Administrative Assistants (43-6013.00)
sources.note: ⚠⚠ The largest of the three routes by employment and the one with no ladder: 850,000 employed, 85,900 annual openings, growth average (3% to 4%), median $45,930 (2025). Education 48% high school diploma, 26% associate degree, 20% postsecondary certificate.

sources.label: AHIMA — RHIT examination eligibility
sources.note: ⚠⚠⚠ The rule the page turns on: a candidate must have successfully completed the academic requirements, at an associate degree level, of a Health Information Management programme accredited by CAHIIM (or an approved foreign equivalent). ⚠⚠ AHIMA further states that HEALTH INFORMATICS degrees are not currently accepted for the RHIT examination — so a certificate does not qualify and neither does the newer-sounding degree.

sources.label: AAPC — removing the CPC-A apprentice designation
sources.note: ⚠⚠⚠ Pass the CPC without qualifying experience and you hold CPC-A. Removal requires verification of TWO YEARS of on-the-job coding experience (externships count), or ONE year plus AAPC's Practicode or its 80-hour medical coding course. Processing takes two to four weeks. ⚠ Employers advertising for a CPC generally mean one without the A.

sources.label: IPEDS Completions 2023 (C2023_A) — CIP 51.07 sub-codes
sources.note: ⚠⚠ The three routes, measured. Health information management (51.0707 + 51.0706): 31 Florida public institutions, 296 credentials, 109 associate and 127 bachelor's. Billing and coding (51.0714): 37 institutions, 416 credentials, ALL certificates. Office administration (51.0716 + 51.0705 + 51.0710 + 51.0702): 36 institutions, 242, all certificates. ⚠ Health care ADMINISTRATION (51.0701) is separate and far larger — 24 institutions, 1,293 credentials, mostly bachelor's and master's.

sources.label: SCNS statewide course file — the HIM prefix
sources.note: ⚠⚠ The level digit separates the routes: HIM0xxx are clock hours, HIM1xxx/HIM2xxx college credit, HIM3xxx/HIM4xxx the bachelor's. ⚠ Two active coder/biller families — HIM0091–0093 at 350+350+320 hours (15 carriers) and HIM0071–0073, OCP B, at 300+300+310 (7), with five institutions carrying both. ⚠⚠⚠ And HIM2222's statewide title still reads BASIC ICD-9-CM CODING, a code set retired in the United States on 1 October 2015, while all six carriers title it ICD-10 work.
